episodes.title: Cut to the Chase! US jobs data bolsters case for September hike, but upcoming CPI more important.
episodes.summary:
**Summary**
Standard Chartered's Jonathan Liang reviews the August US jobs report and flags Friday's CPI print as the more decisive input for the September 16 FOMC decision, with a formal house-view update due September 11. The framing centers on the odds of a Fed hike this cycle, a scenario still seen as tail-risk but rising.

**Key points**
- August US Non-Farm Payrolls printed 162,000 new jobs; unemployment held steady at 4.1%, a resilient labor market backdrop.
- Odds of a September Fed rate hike have risen, reinforced by Fed's Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech.
- StanChart says a core CPI print at or above 0.2% month-on-month this Friday would shift their call from no hikes in 2026 to one September hike; view to be published September 11, ahead of the September 16 FOMC meeting.
- A hike, if delivered, is framed as a Fed credibility move, notable given President Trump's weekend calls for rate cuts.
- StanChart extended its recommended UST duration range from 3-5 years to 3-7 years, expecting intermediate yields to actually fall post-hike as credibility is reasserted; prefers expressing this via 3-7 year US corporate credit (BB-rated or better), citing strong earnings fundamentals and partial avoidance of AI-related long-end supply that is widening spreads further out the curve.

**FX / rates implications**
- A September Fed hike would likely support USD/DXY near-term on rate-differential grounds, a headwind for EM Asia and LATAM carry trades (INR, IDR, PHP, MXN, BRL) even as US intermediate yields are expected to compress on credibility grounds.
- Politically charged Fed independence narrative (Trump vs. Warsh/FOMC) is a risk-sentiment wildcard that could add volatility to EM FX regardless of the actual rate decision.
- Steeper focus on 3-7yr UST/credit vs. long end signals relative value in belly-of-curve positioning, relevant for EM rates traders benchmarking against UST curve shape.

**Watch list**
- US CPI report, Friday September 11 (core MoM at/above 0.2% is the hike trigger threshold).
- StanChart's updated rate-call publication, September 11.
- FOMC meeting, September 16 (US time).
